## Introduction

### Why This Report Exists---Rationale {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Intro subsections are unnumbered and kept out of the table of contents, so the
report opens like an essay. Citations appear in the margin [@tufte2001].

![](images/cover.jpg){.lv-float-right}

A small image with `.lv-float-right` (or `.lv-float-left`) floats beside the
text and drops onto its own line on phones. Margin notes work too.^[Footnotes
appear in the margin because the format sets `reference-location: margin`.]

### How I Kept Score---Data and Methods {.unnumbered .unlisted}

A short, plain-language account of the data and methods. Detailed definitions
belong in a Technical Notes section near the end.

## Findings {#sec-findings}

### A Figure

```{r example-figure}
#| label: fig-example
#| fig-cap: "Captions sit above the figure and carry the explanation. The first sentence becomes the entry in the List of Figures and Tables."

ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(color = brand_color("blue-dark"), size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = brand_color("pink")) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = 5, y = 30, label = "HEAVIER CARS, FEWER MILES",
    fontface = "bold", size = 3, color = brand_color("ink")
  ) +
  labs(x = "Weight (1,000 lb)", y = "Miles per gallon")
```

### A Table

```{r example-table}
#| label: tbl-example
#| tbl-cap: "Tables use lv_table(): monospace numbers, hairline rules, and flush-left placement."

mtcars |>
  group_by(Cylinders = cyl) |>
  summarise(Cars = n(), `Mean MPG` = round(mean(mpg), 1)) |>
  lv_table(width = 0.6, notes = "Source: mtcars.")
```
